title: Impact of IPO Lockup Expiry on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study. The IPO lockup expiry date is known in advance and is common across firms relative to their own event time. We estimate abnormal returns (AR) by subtracting market-model expected returns (using provided betas) and cumulate them in windows around the event to obtain CAR. The average CAR across stocks is tested against zero.

Key assumptions:
- Market model is correctly specified over the short event window (AR = ret − beta × mkt_ret captures expected return).
- No confounding firm-specific events are systematically clustered at the lockup expiry.
- Short-window event-time independence: any anticipation or leakage is limited; pre-event ARs should be near zero.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Required packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
})

options(scipen = 999, digits = 4)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s57_data.csv"
df <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2) Construct abnormal returns
# Market-model abnormal return using provided beta (assumes alpha ~ 0 over short window)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(AR_mm  = ret - beta * mkt_ret,
         AR_mar = ret - mkt_ret)  # robustness: market-adjusted (beta=1)

# 3) Helper functions
winsorize <- function(x, p = 0.01) {
  q <- quantile(x, probs = c(p, 1 - p), na.rm = TRUE)
  pmin(pmax(x, q[1]), q[2])
}

car_stats <- function(data, ar_col, win) {
  # Compute CAR by stock over a given window (sum of ARs over days in window)
  tmp <- data %>%
    filter(event_day >= win[1], event_day <= win[2]) %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    summarise(CAR = sum(.data[[ar_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
              n_days = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n_days > 0)  # keep stocks with at least one day in window

  N <- nrow(tmp)
  mean_car <- mean(tmp$CAR, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd_car   <- sd(tmp$CAR, na.rm = TRUE)
  se_car   <- sd_car / sqrt(N)
  t_stat   <- ifelse(se_car > 0, mean_car / se_car, NA_real_)
  p_val    <- ifelse(is.na(t_stat), NA_real_, 2 * pt(-abs(t_stat), df = N - 1))
  ci_low   <- mean_car - qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * se_car
  ci_high  <- mean_car + qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * se_car

  list(N = N, mean = mean_car, t = t_stat, p = p_val, ci = c(ci_low, ci_high))
}

print_car_results <- function(label, res, win) {
  cat(sprintf("%s CAR [%d,%d]: N=%d  Mean=%0.4f  t=%0.2f  p=%0.3f  95%% CI=[%0.4f,%0.4f]\n",
              label, win[1], win[2], res$N, res$mean, res$t, res$p, res$ci[1], res$ci[2]))
}

# 4) Main analysis: Event-study CARs using market-model AR
windows <- list(`[-1,1]` = c(-1, 1),
                `[-3,3]` = c(-3, 3),
                `[0,2]`  = c(0, 2),
                `[0,5]`  = c(0, 5))

cat("Main results: Market-model abnormal returns (AR_mm)\n")
main_results <- lapply(windows, function(w) car_stats(df, "AR_mm", w))
invisible(mapply(function(name, w, res) print_car_results(paste0("CAR ", name), res, w),
                 names(windows), windows, main_results))

# Also report average day-0 abnormal return
ar0 <- df %>%
  filter(event_day == 0) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(AR0 = sum(AR_mm, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
if (nrow(ar0) > 1) {
  N0 <- nrow(ar0)
  mean0 <- mean(ar0$AR0)
  sd0 <- sd(ar0$AR0)
  se0 <- sd0 / sqrt(N0)
  t0 <- ifelse(se0 > 0, mean0 / se0, NA_real_)
  p0 <- ifelse(is.na(t0), NA_real_, 2 * pt(-abs(t0), df = N0 - 1))
  ci0 <- c(mean0 - qt(0.975, df = N0 - 1) * se0, mean0 + qt(0.975, df = N0 - 1) * se0)
  cat(sprintf("Day 0 AR: N=%d  Mean=%0.4f  t=%0.2f  p=%0.3f  95%% CI=[%0.4f,%0.4f]\n",
              N0, mean0, t0, p0, ci0[1], ci0[2]))
}

# 5) Robustness checks

cat("\nRobustness 1: Market-adjusted returns (AR_mar = ret - mkt_ret)\n")
rob1 <- lapply(windows, function(w) car_stats(df, "AR_mar", w))
invisible(mapply(function(name, w, res) print_car_results(paste0("CAR ", name), res, w),
                 names(windows), windows, rob1))

cat("\nRobustness 2: Winsorized AR_mm at 1% tails\n")
df_w <- df %>% mutate(AR_mm_w = winsorize(AR_mm, p = 0.01))
rob2 <- lapply(windows, function(w) car_stats(df_w, "AR_mm_w", w))
invisible(mapply(function(name, w, res) print_car_results(paste0("CAR ", name), res, w),
                 names(windows), windows, rob2))

cat("\nRobustness 3: Placebo pre-event window CAR [-10,-6] (should be ~0)\n")
placebo_win <- c(-10, -6)
placebo <- car_stats(df, "AR_mm", placebo_win)
print_car_results("Placebo", placebo, placebo_win)

cat("\nRobustness 4: Pre-trend check, average AR over [-5,-2]\n")
pre_win <- c(-5, -2)
pre <- car_stats(df, "AR_mm", pre_win)
print_car_results("Pre-AR mean", pre, pre_win)

cat("\nAnalysis complete.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative abnormal performance around lockup expiry due to increased float and potential insider selling pressure.
- Magnitude: Average CAR roughly −1% to −2% over [-1,+1], and −2% to −4% over [0,+5]. Day 0 AR typically negative (around −0.5% to −1.5%).
- The placebo and pre-trend windows should be near zero and statistically insignificant; robustness using market-adjusted returns and winsorization should yield similar negative CARs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare CAR before and after lockup expiry.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The lockup expiry leads to a negative impact on CAR.
